subject: Maths
title: Dividing in a ratio
subtitle: Ratio · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can divide a quantity in a given ratio.

key_vocab.definition: splitting a total into parts according to a given ratio. Find the total number of parts first.
Add the ratio parts. Divide the total by this sum to find one part. Multiply to find each share.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can divide a quantity in a given ratio.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content:
Dividing in a ratio -- splitting a total into parts according to a given ratio. Find the total number of parts first.
Method -- Add the ratio parts. Divide the total by this sum to find one part. Multiply to find each share.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Add ratio parts. Divide total by number of parts. Multiply each ratio number by value of one part.
Total ÷ (a + b) = 1 part
Then multiply: a parts and b parts

Key examples:
  ✓ £20 in ratio 3:2 = £12 and £8  (5 parts, £4 each)
  ✓ Ratio 1:3 means one quarter and three quarters  (fractions of total)
  ✓ Total parts = sum of ratio numbers  (first step)
  ✗ £20 in ratio 3:2 = £10 and £10  (divided equally, not in ratio)
  ✗ Ratio 3:2 means 3 and 2  (must multiply by value per part)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – simple ratio
  Divide £35 in the ratio 3:4.
  Total parts: 3 + 4 = 7
  One part: 35 ÷ 7 = £5
  3 parts = £15, 4 parts = £20
  £15 and £20
  (Check: £15 + £20 = £35.)

Example 2 – three-part ratio
  Divide 60 kg in the ratio 1:2:3.
  Total parts: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6
  One part: 60 ÷ 6 = 10 kg
  Shares: 10 kg, 20 kg, 30 kg
  10 kg, 20 kg, 30 kg
  (Same method works for three or more parts.)

sections.title: Simple two-part ratios
sections.content:
Divide each amount in the given ratio.

(a) £24 in ratio 1:3
(b) £40 in ratio 3:5
(c) 60 cm in ratio 2:3
(d) £100 in ratio 7:3

sections.title: Three-part ratios
sections.content:
Divide in the ratio given.

(a) £60 in ratio 1:2:3
(b) 120 kg in ratio 2:3:5
(c) £180 in ratio 4:5:1
(d) 90 litres in ratio 1:2:6

sections.title: Finding the total or one share
sections.content:
Work backwards from the given information.

(a) Ratio 2:5. Smaller share = £14. Total?
(b) Ratio 4:3. Larger share = £48. Total?
(c) Ratio 5:2. Difference = 21. Total?
(d) Ratio 3:7. Smaller share = 12 kg. Larger share?

sections.title: Word problems
sections.content:
Solve each ratio problem.

(a) 3 friends share £45 in ratio 2:3:4. How much does each get?
(b) Concrete: cement:sand:gravel = 1:2:4. Need 35 kg total. How much sand?
(c) Ages in ratio 3:5. Older is 20 years. How old is younger?
(d) Profit shared 2:3. Total profit £7500. How much more does larger share get?

sections.title: Mixed ratio division
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) £56 in ratio 3:4
(b) £200 in ratio 2:3:5
(c) Ratio 5:8. Difference = £21. Find both shares.
(d) Ratio 1:2:3. Middle share = £30. Total?
(e) Orange juice: water = 2:5. Need 700ml total. How much OJ?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ To divide in ratio 3:2, find total parts (5) first
✗ Ratio 3:2 means divide by 3 and by 2
✓ The shares should always add up to the original total
✗ £20 in ratio 3:2 gives £10 each
✓ Ratio 1:4 means one fifth and four fifths
